subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 2: Grammar – talking about the future
outcomes: Choose the right future form: will, be going to, present continuous or present simple.
Talk about predictions, offers, intentions and arrangements.

tf.s: We use the present simple for timetables and scheduled events: 'The show finishes at 10.'
We use the present continuous for fixed arrangements: 'I'm meeting my aunt at 8 p.m.'
tf.why: An arrangement with a time and place.

tf.s: 'I'll lend you some money' is an offer.
tf.why: Will is used for offers and quick decisions.

tf.s: We use 'be going to' for timetables, like train times.
tf.why: Timetables use the present simple: The train leaves at 7.

tf.s: 'Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.' is a prediction based on what we can see.
tf.why: We use going to when there is evidence now.

tf.s: 'I'm going to clean my room' is an intention.
tf.why: Be going to shows a plan you have decided.

tf.s: 'The flight arriving at 7 tomorrow' is correct.
tf.why: We need a verb form: 'The flight arrives / is arriving at 7.'

tf.s: We use 'will' after 'I think' for predictions: 'I think it will rain.'
tf.why: I think + will is a common prediction.

tf.s: 'Many people going to her shows' is a correct prediction.
tf.why: We say: Many people will go to her shows.

tf.s: The present continuous can only talk about now, never the future.
tf.why: It can also talk about future arrangements.

boxes.why: Scheduled events use the present simple.

mcq.q: Which set shows an arrangement, an intention and a prediction in that order?
o: I'm visiting Gran on Friday. / I'm going to clean my room. / I think it will rain.
I think it will rain. / I'm visiting Gran. / I'll help you.
I'll help you. / The bus leaves at 6. / I'm going to study.
